test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In August 2025, the report ‘Unlocking a $200 Billion Opportunity: Electric Vehicles in India,’ assessing challenges and key steps for India’s Electric Mobility transition, was released by ________.

options.text: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled ‘**Unlocking a $200 Billion Opportunity: Electric Vehicles in India**’ was released by **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India) in **August 2025** to provide a roadmap for the country’s transition toward **Electric Mobility**.
 
• This comprehensive study was developed in collaboration with **RMI** (Rocky Mountain Institute) and **RMI India** to assess the capital requirements and financing challenges in the **Electric Vehicle (EV)** sector.
 
• The report highlights that India requires a cumulative investment of **$200 billion** (approximately **Rs 14.37 lakh crore**) by the **year 2030** to achieve its targets for vehicle production, **charging infrastructure**, and battery manufacturing.
 
• It identifies that the **transition to electric vehicles** is not just an environmental necessity but a massive economic opportunity that can reduce **oil imports** and position India as a global manufacturing hub.
 
• The primary focus of the report is on **mobilizing private capital** and identifying the **financing gap** that exists for retail **EV loans**, which is crucial for the **2-wheeler** and **3-wheeler** segments. *Hence, the statement regarding NITI Aayog being the releasing authority is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **FAME-II Scheme**: The **Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid &) Electric Vehicles** (FAME) India Phase II was launched by the **Ministry of Heavy Industries** with a significant **budgetary outlay** to subsidize **EV purchases** and support **charging stations**.
 
• **PLI Scheme for ACC**: The **Government of India** introduced a **Production Linked Incentive (PLI)** scheme for **Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC)** battery storage with an investment of **Rs 18,100 crore** to boost domestic manufacturing and reduce dependency on **imports**.
 
• **2030 EV Ambition**: India aims to achieve **30%** electric vehicle penetration for **private cars**, **70%** for **commercial vehicles**, and **80%** for **two and three-wheelers** by the **year 2030**.
 
• **e-AMRIT Portal**: **NITI Aayog** launched the **e-AMRIT** (Accelerated e-Mobility Revolution for India’s Transportation) web portal during the **COP26 summit** to serve as a **one-stop-shop** for all information regarding **electric vehicles** in **India**.
 
• **GST Benefits**: To encourage **consumers**, the **GST Council** reduced the tax rate on **Electric Vehicles** from **12%** to **5%**, and on **chargers/charging stations** from **18%** to **5%**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Priority Sector Lending (PSL)**: One of the key recommendations in such **NITI Aayog** reports is the inclusion of **Electric Vehicles** under the **Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI)** **Priority Sector Lending** guidelines to ensure **low-cost financing**.
 
• **Economic Impact**: Achieving the **$200 billion** investment target is estimated to reduce **carbon dioxide emissions** significantly and save billions in **foreign exchange** by reducing **crude oil** demand.
 
• **Infrastructure Requirements**: The report emphasizes that **India** will need approximately **2.9 million** public **charging points** by **2030** to support the projected growth of the **EV fleet**.
 
• **State-Level Policies**: Various **States** like **Delhi**, **Maharashtra**, and **Karnataka** have released their own **EV policies** providing **road tax exemptions** and **registration fee waivers** to supplement **Central Government** efforts.
</ul
